commitResults.messageTitle: Add guardian follow-ups to the student model
commitResults.messageBody:
Tutors often promise guardians something after a lesson, such as a
progress report or a make-up slot, but StudentBook has nowhere to
record these, so they are easy to forget (user stories 35, 36, 43
and 44).

Let's,
* add a FollowUp holding 1-200 characters of single-line text
* keep a student's outstanding follow-ups in an ordered list
* save them as a followUps array in the data file
* pass the existing follow-ups on in every command that rebuilds a
  student, so editing other fields never drops them

Archiving rebuilds the student through Student#withArchived, which
passes an empty list for notes, so archiving a student loses their
progress notes. Let's make it keep both notes and follow-ups.

Follow-ups belong to the student, not the guardian, so deleting a
guardian keeps them and a student without a guardian can still have
them. Completing an item will remove it, so every stored item is
outstanding and no "done" flag is needed.

Data files without followUps still load, with no follow-ups.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
Claude-Session: https://claude.ai/code/session_01XU83rHRq156PAaihRT3jCB

commitResults.messageTitle: Add commands to manage guardian follow-ups
commitResults.messageBody:
Follow-ups can be stored on a student, but there is no way to add,
change, complete or list them from the command box.

Let's add,
* followup-add STUDENT_INDEX text/TEXT
* followup-edit STUDENT_INDEX FOLLOW_UP_INDEX text/TEXT
* followup-done STUDENT_INDEX FOLLOW_UP_INDEX, which removes the item
* followups, which lists only students with outstanding items

The commands follow the operation-based pattern of the lesson,
guardian and note commands. Text that matches another of the
student's items ignoring case is rejected as a duplicate. Success
messages include the item's text, so a wrong index is noticed at once.

After followups, completing a student's last item removes them from
the list and renumbers the rest, so the student's details are opened
at their new position, or not at all, rather than at a stale index.

commitResults.messageTitle: Accept common phone formats with 7 to 15 digits
commitResults.messageBody:
Phone numbers must be plain digits, at least 3 long. Common Singapore
formats such as 9123 4567 and +65 9123 4567 are rejected, while 3-digit
and 40-digit numbers are accepted. Guardian phones share the rule.

Tutors cannot type numbers the way parents give them, yet obviously
wrong numbers get saved.

Let's,
* accept an optional leading + and single spaces or hyphens between
  groups of digits
* require 7 to 15 digits, the earlier specification's range and the
  international maximum
* save the number without its spaces and hyphens

Saving only digits keeps 9123 4567 and 91234567 equal, so a guardian
search for 91234567 still finds a number entered as 9123 4567.

A data file holding a phone with fewer than 7 digits no longer loads.
Sample data and the seeder use 8-digit numbers.

Fixes #186.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

commitResults.messageTitle: Reject note dates before the year 2000
commitResults.messageBody:
note-add accepts any real date that is not in the future, so a
mistyped year such as 0026-10-15 is saved.

The note then sorts first as the oldest note, and the numbers of the
student's other notes shift, so later note-delete commands can hit
the wrong note.

Let's reject note dates earlier than 2000-01-01 with their own error
message, alongside the existing check for future dates.

A tutor's lesson notes are not expected to predate 2000, so the bound
catches mistyped years without blocking real notes. Saved notes are not
checked, so existing data files still load.

Fixes #187.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

commitResults.messageTitle: Collapse repeated spaces in follow-up text
commitResults.messageBody:
Follow-up text keeps repeated spaces between words, so Call  mum and
call mum are both accepted as separate follow-ups, although the
duplicate check already ignores letter case.

The student ends up with two copies of the same task.

Let's collapse repeated spaces in follow-up text before it is checked
and saved, for both followup-add and followup-edit.

This matches how names have treated repeated spaces since #178.

Fixes #188.

commitResults.messageTitle: Warn about lesson clashes when unarchiving a student
commitResults.messageBody:
Archived lessons are only checked against other archived lessons, so
unarchive could double-book the tutor without a warning. It now checks
each returning lesson against the active students, as lesson-add does,
and still unarchives the student.

commitResults.messageTitle: Keep add showing the new student during a search
commitResults.messageBody:
AddCommand selects the new student by its place in the shown list, so add
must still clear the active search. Without that, adding a student who does
not match the search threw IndexOutOfBoundsException.

Add tests that archive and unarchive keep both searches, and correct the
guides to say add is the exception.
